questions.question: A patient has chromoblastomycosis.

parts.text: What is the name of the cells classically seen on microscopy of the lesion?

parts_raw.text: What is the name of the cells classically seen on gram stain of the lesion?

questions.model_answer:
a) Muriform (sclerotic) cells, also called Medlar bodies or copper-penny bodies; classically seen in KOH preparations of skin scrapings (often within black dots) and on H&E-stained biopsy, not on Gram stain.
b) (1) Fonsecaea pedrosoi (most common agent). (2) Fonsecaea compacta. (3) Cladophialophora (Cladosporium) carrionii.
c) (1) Itraconazole (100-400 mg/day, often with adjunctive cryotherapy). (2) Terbinafine (500 mg/day). (3) Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen (alone for small early lesions or combined with an azole); posaconazole is an alternative for itraconazole/terbinafine-refractory disease.

cohort_answer.text: Muriform cells / Medlar bodies / copper penny cells. || Fonsecaea pedrosoi; Fonsecaea compacta; Cladophialophora carrionii (usually occurs in tropical/subtropical areas, associated with farming/decaying vegetation, transmission by traumatic inoculation; non-painful, pruritic, raised scaly, warty/cauliflower-like appearance occurring weeks-months after trauma). || Itraconazole; Terbinafine; Cryo + liquid nitrogen; Posaconazole.
